title: SBAR call to raise a concern about a prescribed medicine
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
The ISMP list is used only to justify choosing a high-alert medicine as the example; no medicine guidance is given.
The example names no medicine, dose or route.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Raise a medicine concern clearly without blame.
Name the specific concern and ask for a decision.

sources.use: ISMP high-alert list: used only to say that some medicines need extra care

required_sources: A professional standard on questioning a prescription
setup: A fictional adult in a fictional ICU bed on a continuous infusion; a proposed new medicine order differs from the expected plan. The nurse seeks immediate clarification before implementing the change, while ensuring existing essential therapy is not abruptly interrupted.

items.text: I am calling about Ms B in bed 7. I have an order I would like to check before I give it.
items.why: It says why you are calling.

items.text: She had a procedure this morning, and her previous order was different.
items.why: It gives relevant context for the query.

items.text: The new order does not match what I expected, and I am not confident it is intended.
items.why: It states your concern and its basis without blame.

items.text: Please clarify the new order urgently. I will not implement the unconfirmed change; we need a safe interim plan for the currently running infusion.
items.why: A specific request for clarification and a clinician-directed interim plan; avoid abruptly stopping essential ongoing support.

items.text: The last doctor never writes clearly.
items.why: Blame does not help the decision.

items.text: She has no known drug allergies on her chart, and this is the same class of medicine she was on before the procedure.
items.why: It is relevant background the prescriber needs to judge the query, without naming a medicine or a dose.

items.text: The infusion pump is already programmed for the previous order and has not been changed yet.
items.why: It communicates the current equipment state. The team must assess whether the existing therapy remains safe; the previous pump setting is not automatically safe.
